contentBlocks.title: Report on Free Access to Educational Resources Through the University Library Website

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) promotes inclusive access to knowledge and educational resources through its well-established Library and Information Centre. In addition to catering to the academic and research requirements of its students and faculty members, the University makes a wide range of educational resources accessible to the general public through its official Library website.

The online library portal serves as an open gateway to diverse academic and informational resources, enabling students, researchers, academicians and members of the public to access educational materials free of cost. This initiative extends the University's knowledge-sharing commitment beyond its campus and supports independent learning, academic exploration and lifelong learning.

contentBlocks.title: University Library Collection & Open Access Infrastructure
rows: Digital resource-platform links listed on the Library website

contentBlocks.text: 1. Availability of Library Resources: The University maintains an extensive library collection comprising more than 1,75,000 resources, including books, reference materials, journals, magazines, newspapers, research publications and digital resources across 6 campus libraries with 134 computer systems and a total seating capacity of 1,018.

2. Free Access to Digital Educational Resources: The University's Library website provides direct links to 42 digital educational resource platforms covering different academic disciplines and areas of general interest, accessible without requiring paid subscriptions or institutional membership.

contentBlocks.title: Prominent Open Educational Platforms Accessible via Library Portal

contentBlocks.text: 4. Access to Institutional and Scholarly Databases: The University Library website also provides information and links to reputed national and international academic databases and electronic information resources, including EBSCO, Springer, JSTOR, ProQuest, J-Gate, N-List and Scopus.

5. Additional Digital Learning and Information Resources: E-newspapers (The Hindu, Deccan Herald, Times of India, Deccan Chronicle, Economic Times), E-magazines (India Today, Business Today, Outlook, Digit, Reader's Digest), General Knowledge and Current Affairs resources, and Institutional Research Repositories.

contentBlocks.title: Report on Open Access Educational Content Made Available to the General Public

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University has undertaken a distinctive and commendable initiative by making a substantial collection of faculty-developed educational resources freely accessible to the general public through digital platforms. This initiative reflects the University's progressive vision of democratizing education, promoting knowledge sharing and extending the benefits of higher education beyond conventional campus boundaries.

1. Video-Based Educational Resources: The University has made 156 educational video resources available through online platforms, particularly YouTube. These videos cover Accounting and Finance, Economics and Commerce, Management and Professional Management Studies, Psychology and Social Sciences, Forensic Science, Life Sciences, English, Kannada, Hindi, and Media Studies.

2. Other Digital Educational Content: In addition to video lectures, the University has facilitated access to 63 other digital educational resources through online platforms, including presentations, academic materials, subject-specific learning content, interactive exercises and knowledge-sharing modules.

3. Public Accessibility and Impact: Providing free and open access to 219 educational resources (156 video resources and 63 digital learning materials) is an exemplary model of inclusive, technology-enabled, and socially responsible higher education.

contentBlocks.title: Institutional Certificate Courses Open to Learners
1. Certificate Course on Sports Nutrition (1 September – 30 October 2025)
paragraphs: Objective: To provide participants with fundamental knowledge of sports nutrition, dietary requirements, nutritional planning and the role of balanced nutrition in enhancing physical performance, fitness and overall well-being.

Write-up: The Centre for Physical Education and Fitness, in collaboration with the Department of Life Sciences, organized a Certificate Course on Sports Nutrition from 1 September to 30 October 2025. The programme focused on the significance of nutrition in sports performance, physical fitness and health management, equipping participants with an understanding of essential nutrients, dietary planning, hydration, energy requirements and nutritional strategies for physical activities. Certificates of completion were awarded to successful participants.

contentBlocks.title: 2. Certificate Course on Competency Mapping (8 – 26 September 2025)
paragraphs: Objective: To develop an understanding of competency mapping and its application in identifying, assessing and developing individual competencies for improved personal, academic and professional effectiveness.

Write-up: The Department of Psychology, School of Humanities and Social Sciences, organized a Certificate Course on Competency Mapping from 8 to 26 September 2025. The programme introduced participants to the concept, significance and practical applications of competency mapping, identifying individual strengths, assessing behavioural competencies, and aligning individual capabilities with organizational and professional expectations. Certificates of completion were awarded to participants.

contentBlocks.title: 3. Certificate Course on Voices from the Margins: Exploring Indigenous (Dalit and Tribal) Narratives (15 September – 18 October 2025)
paragraphs: Objective: To introduce participants to indigenous, Dalit and tribal narratives and develop an understanding of marginalized voices, cultural identities, social realities and literary representations through critical engagement with diverse texts and perspectives.

Write-up: The Department of English, School of Humanities and Social Sciences, organized a 30-hour Certificate Course titled Voices from the Margins: Exploring Indigenous (Dalit and Tribal) Narratives from 15 September to 18 October 2025. The programme explored themes of social justice, identity, representation, cultural heritage and inclusion. As part of the programme, an expert session on Dalit Poetry was delivered by Dr. Abhisarika Prajapati, Associate Professor and Head, Department of English, REVA University, Bengaluru, on 19 September 2025. Certificates of completion and appreciation were awarded to participants and resource persons.

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University, through its various centers and cells, organized several programs and initiatives on campus during the academic year 2025–2026. These activities focused on community service, women's empowerment, social inclusion, health awareness and inclusive communication, providing opportunities for students, volunteers and the public to engage in socially meaningful initiatives.

contentBlocks.title: 1. Computer Literacy Programme for Slum and Migrant Children (12 September 2025)
paragraphs: On 12 September 2025, JES conducted a computer literacy program for children from slum and migrant communities. The program aimed to improve digital awareness and introduce basic computer skills among underprivileged children.

A total of 28 students participated in the initiative and received an opportunity to develop basic computer knowledge and familiarity with technology. The program focused on promoting digital inclusion and providing children with essential technological skills to support their educational development.

contentBlocks.title: 2. SRUJANA – Art, Craft and Food Stall (26 August 2025)
paragraphs: On 26 August 2025, the Women Empowerment Cell organized an art, craft and food stall under the SRUJANA initiative on the university campus. The program aimed to encourage creativity, develop entrepreneurial skills and provide a platform for showcasing products created by participants.

The stall featured a variety of art and craft items alongside food products, highlighting the creative abilities and practical skills of the individuals involved. A total of 22 center volunteers actively contributed to organizing and managing the stalls, while the program recorded a reach of 130 participants. It promoted awareness of small-scale entrepreneurial activities and self-employment opportunities.

contentBlocks.title: 3. SRUJANA – Art, Craft and Food Stall (24 October 2025)
paragraphs: On 24 October 2025, the Women Empowerment Cell organized another edition of the SRUJANA art, craft and food stall on the university campus. The initiative aimed to promote creativity, encourage entrepreneurial thinking and provide opportunities for showcasing artistic talents and practical skills.

A total of 76 center volunteers actively contributed to the planning, coordination and management of the stalls, ensuring the smooth conduct of the program. The event recorded a reach of 190 participants, who visited the stalls, explored handmade craft products and interacted with the volunteers, supporting creative expression and women's empowerment.

contentBlocks.title: 4. Campuspreneurs 2025 (23 September 2025)
paragraphs: The Department of Management, School of Business and Management, Kristu Jayanti University, organized Campuspreneurs 2025, a stall-based entrepreneurial exhibition, on 23 September 2025 for III BBA students.

A total of 16 exhibits involving 96 student participants were showcased, attracting approximately 420 visitors to the exhibition hall. The stalls featured eco-friendly products, sustainable lifestyle items, herbal personal care, handmade décor, games, and food items. The exhibition provided practical exposure to entrepreneurial decision-making, marketing, pricing, sales, and consumer behaviour.

contentBlocks.title: 5. Campus Farmers' Market – Vegetable and Fruits Mela (29 August 2025)
paragraphs: The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) of Kristu Jayanti University organized the Campus Farmers’ Market – Vegetable and Fruits Mela on 29 August 2025 as part of the Viksit Bharat @ 2047 initiative.

The program aimed to promote direct engagement between farmers and consumers, encourage community-based agricultural enterprise and support local products under the Government of India’s One District One Product (ODOP) initiative. The market featured Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) from Chitradurga, Vijayapura and Chintamani, along with Greenkraft Producer Company Limited, showcasing fresh agricultural produce to over 75 resident consumers, eliminating intermediaries and ensuring fair returns.

contentBlocks.title: 1. Professional Development Programme on Empowering Institutions for Sustainable Excellence
paragraphs: Date: 19–20 September 2025 | Venue: Council Room, Admin Block | Beneficiaries: 22 Teachers from Christ School, Hassan

The Office of Human Resources organised a two-day Professional Development Programme for 22 teachers from Christ School, Hassan. The programme aimed to enhance teaching competencies, classroom management, student mentoring and leadership skills.

Faculty members conducted sessions on growth-oriented teaching perspectives, innovative classroom management, effective student mentoring, teamwork, institutional collaboration and inspirational leadership, accompanied by campus visits and interactions with the Vice Chancellor.

contentBlocks.title: 2. Professional Development Programme on Institutional Development and University Status
paragraphs: Date: 12 November 2025 | Venue: Council Room, Admin Block | Beneficiaries: 14 Officials from Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology, Ernakulam

The Office of Human Resources facilitated an institutional interaction for 14 officials from Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology to provide insights into academic, administrative, governance and quality assurance practices involved in attaining university status.

The interaction featured meetings with the Vice Chancellor and the IQAC team on institutional documentation, academic records management, quality monitoring, accreditation procedures and regulatory compliance, concluding with a guided campus tour.

contentBlocks.title: 3. Professional Development Programme on Institutional Development and University Status
paragraphs: Date: 15 November 2025 | Venue: Council Room, Admin Block | Beneficiaries: Principal and 11 Faculty Members (12 Total) from St. Agnes College (Autonomous), Mangalore

The Office of Human Resources organised an institutional interaction for the Principal and faculty members of St. Agnes College, focusing on university governance, statutory requirements, examination reforms, curriculum frameworks and IQAC accreditation strategies.
Dr. Aloysius Edward (Registrar) and Prof. Geo Joy (Controller of Examinations) addressed statutory frameworks, curriculum design, academic autonomy, and examination management systems.

contentBlocks.title: 4. Professional Development Programme on Fostering Institutional Excellence
paragraphs: Date: 29–30 April 2025 | Organised by: Human Resource Development Centre | Beneficiaries: 21 Educators from Carmel Public School, Puliyanmala, Kerala

The two-day training featured expert sessions on developing a growth-oriented teaching mindset, interpersonal effectiveness, classroom management, student mentoring, and empowering leadership in schools, facilitated by senior university academic leaders.

contentBlocks.title: 5. Leadership Development Programme on School Management and Enhancing Institutional Effectiveness
paragraphs: Date: 26–27 May 2025 | Organised by: Human Resource Development Centre | Beneficiaries: 18 Educational Leaders from Little Flower Mission Education Society

The programme covered the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, NCRF, academic budgeting, AI tools in education, transformational leadership, stakeholder engagement, and student-centred learning models.

indicators.subtitle: Centre for Community Education (CCE) & 49 Beyond-Campus Educational Outreach Initiatives

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University has established the Centre for Community Education (CCE) as a flagship initiative dedicated exclusively to community education and outreach. The Centre serves as a platform for extending the University's educational resources, knowledge, expertise and institutional support to the wider community. It focuses on promoting inclusive learning, social awareness, skill development, capacity building and lifelong learning opportunities, particularly among underserved and marginalized sections of society.

During the year 2025, the University conducted 49 extensive outreach initiatives beyond the campus connecting students and faculty with schools, rural and urban communities, care institutions, migrant settlements, and public spaces.

contentBlocks.title: Major Areas of Community Achievement
rows: Awareness initiatives addressing women’s health, menstrual hygiene, dengue prevention, mental health, nutrition, healthcare, first aid, and child safety.
Programmes focusing on rural education and literacy campaigns, values and life skills, IT education, study-material support, and learning initiatives.
Village-level engagement including rural exposure camps, village surveys, Shramadhaan, and community initiatives in adopted and neighbouring villages.
Cleanliness drives and Swachh Bharat / Swachhata Hi Seva activities encouraging civic participation and responsibility for cleaner public spaces.
Visits and service initiatives at elders’ homes, special schools, migrant settlements, and underprivileged communities.
NCC, KCDC, ABHA card enrollment drives, government scheme awareness, safety, discipline, and civic responsibility.

contentBlocks.title: Comprehensive Write-ups of All 49 Outreach Activities
1. Fostering Women’s Safety and Self Awareness
paragraphs:
An extension activity focusing on women’s safety and well-being was conducted on 9 April 2025 at The
Refuge Foundation, Anjanapura Layout, Bengaluru. The programme witnessed the participation of 8
students from the University and benefited 20 external participants. The initiative aimed to create
awareness about personal safety, self-awareness and confidence among women. It emphasised the
importance of recognising potential risks, developing a sense of personal security and responding
appropriately to situations that may affect their safety and well-being. The programme provided an
opportunity for students to engage with the community and contribute towards promoting awareness and
social responsibility.

contentBlocks.title: 2. Serving with love: visit to the Elders Home
paragraphs:
An outreach visit was organised on 9 September 2025 to the Home for the Aged (Women), Society of
St. Vincent De Paul, Ramaiah Layout, Bengaluru. A total of 14 students from the University participated
in the initiative, which reached 5 elderly residents. The visit provided an opportunity for students to
interact with the residents, offer companionship and understand their social and emotional needs. The
interaction helped nurture empathy, compassion and respect towards senior citizens while reinforcing
the importance of social responsibility and care for the elderly.

contentBlocks.title: 3. Clean Drive in the School
paragraphs:
The event was conducted on 17 september 2025, as an extension activity on the theme of activity. The
activity encouraged cleanliness, civic responsibility and community participation. A total of 16 student
participant(s) from the University took part. The activity was held at Siddhartha School Narayanpura,
Bengaluru. External participants/beneficiaries were recorded as Students and Tecahers of the school.
The activity encouraged collective responsibility for cleanliness and the upkeep of shared spaces. Direct
participation sensitised students to hygiene, civic responsibility and sustained community action.

initiative focused on community awareness and engagement around the subject identified in the event

Mission, 5th Cr, KRC Rd, Doddagubbi, Bengaluru, Karnataka. External participants/beneficiaries were
recorded as the women of New Ark Mission. The programme addressed menstrual health and hygiene
through awareness and information sharing, encouraging informed choices and healthy practices.

contentBlocks.title: KRISTU JAYANTI UNIVERSITY — LIFELONG LEARNING POLICY
contentBlocks.subtitle: Comprehensive Institutional Policy Ensuring Equal and Non-Discriminatory Access to Educational Opportunities
contentBlocks.meta: Approved by University Governing Authorities • Applicable Across All Academic & Extension Units

contentBlocks.title: 1. Preamble and Policy Statement
paragraphs: Kristu Jayanti University recognizes lifelong learning as a continuous process through which individuals acquire, update and apply knowledge, skills, values and competencies throughout their lives. Learning may take place through formal education, professional development, short-term courses, online learning, workplace experience, community engagement and independent study.

In a changing social, economic and technological environment, lifelong learning supports personal growth, employability, innovation, civic participation and institutional development. The Institution is committed to creating inclusive, flexible and quality-assured opportunities for students, faculty, staff, alumni and eligible members of the wider community. This policy is guided by equitable access, learner-centred education, continuous professional development, digital inclusion and continuous improvement.

contentBlocks.title: 2. Purpose and 3. Scope
paragraphs: Purpose: To establish a clear framework for planning, delivering, facilitating, monitoring and improving lifelong learning opportunities beyond the requirements of a single academic programme or qualification.

Scope: Applies to current students, research scholars, faculty members, administrative staff, alumni, working professionals, adult learners, and community members participating in approved learning initiatives without discrimination.

contentBlocks.title: 4. Objectives of Lifelong Learning Policy
paragraphs: • To provide equitable, inclusive and non-discriminatory access to relevant learning opportunities regardless of ethnicity, religion, disability, immigration status or gender.
• To promote continuous upskilling, reskilling, interdisciplinary learning and transferable competencies.
• To offer flexible learning formats, including online, blended, face-to-face, evening and weekend delivery wherever feasible.
• To support professional growth of faculty and staff through training, development programmes, peer learning and exposure to emerging practices.
• To enable students and alumni to continue learning, strengthen employability and adapt to changing career and societal needs.
• To encourage entrepreneurship, innovation, research awareness, digital literacy and responsible use of technology.
• To extend learning opportunities to communities through outreach, extension activities and collaboration with external organisations.
• To maintain quality, relevance and accountability through periodic review, learner feedback and outcome assessment.

contentBlocks.title: 5. Guiding Principles
paragraphs: • Inclusivity and equity: Learning opportunities should be accessible without discrimination. Reasonable accommodation is provided for learners with disabilities.
• Learner-centredness: Curriculum design responds to learners' prior knowledge, goals and circumstances.
• Flexibility: Delivery formats accommodate working professionals and adult learners with diverse schedules.
• Quality and relevance: Clear learning outcomes, competent facilitators and quality assessment standards.
• Digital enablement: High-standard digital infrastructure, repositories, and learning platforms.
• Continuous improvement: Regular outcome assessment, participant feedback and evidence-based curriculum updates.

contentBlocks.title: 6. Policy Framework and Key Provisions (6.1 – 6.8)
paragraphs: 6.1 Lifelong Learning Opportunities: Developing short-term certificates, diplomas, workshops, seminars, staff development, digital literacy, and community awareness programmes.
6.2 Flexible Modes and Learning Pathways: Face-to-face, online, and blended modular delivery schedules.
6.3 Learning Resources and Technology: Public access to digital libraries, repositories, open courses, and LMS platforms.
6.4 Faculty and Staff Development: Institutional sponsorship and continuous pedagogical upskilling.
6.5 Alumni and Community Engagement: Active partnerships with NGOs, industry bodies, and community organizations.
6.6 Inclusion and Learner Support: Reducing financial, geographical, and physical barriers through scholarships, fee concessions, and accessible learning aids.
6.7 Recognition of Prior Learning and Credentials: Transparent certification validating skills and vocational proficiencies.
6.8 Quality Assurance: Rigorous quality benchmarking overseen by the IQAC.

contentBlocks.title: 7. Roles, Responsibilities, Implementation, and Review (Sections 7 – 12)
paragraphs: Governance & IQAC: Governed by the Academic Council and monitored periodically by IQAC to ensure adherence to national statutory guidelines.
Monitoring and Evaluation: Comprehensive evaluation of participant reach, completion rates, learner feedback, and accessibility metrics.
Funding & Ethics: Budgetary allocations support community learning, outreach concessions, and digital infrastructure while upholding strict academic integrity and data privacy.
Review Schedule: Mandatory review every three years to incorporate evolving educational standards and technology developments.

indicators.subtitle: Institutional Enrolment, Mentorship, and Financial Support for First-Generation Learners

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) actively encourages and supports students who are the first in their families to pursue higher education. Dedicated admission counselling, need-based fee concessions, bridge courses, peer-mentoring circles, and academic tutoring ensure smooth transition and successful completion for first-generation learners.
